method: Signals clustered: after a signal fires, the next 63 trading days are skipped so each episode counts once. Only signals with a full forward window are counted.

setups.title: Market falls 10% from its 52-week high
setups.takeaway: The classic correction. Buying fear has the best base rate in the database.

setups.title: Market falls 20% from its 52-week high
setups.takeaway: Bear-market territory. Deep drawdowns have historically been the best buying opportunities.

setups.title: New 52-week high
setups.takeaway: Strength begets strength more often than the 'buy low' crowd admits.

setups.title: Three straight down months
setups.takeaway: Rare and miserable — and historically a launchpad, not a trapdoor.

setups.title: Single-day drop of 3% or more
setups.takeaway: Panic days tend to get bought within a quarter.

setups.title: Single-day rally of 3% or more
setups.takeaway: Explosive up days usually mark panic bottoms, not tops.

setups.title: Closes below the 200-day average (first break)
setups.takeaway: Counterintuitive: since 2010, losing the trend line has usually marked fear worth buying, not the start of something worse.

setups.title: Reclaims the 200-day average after 20+ days below
setups.takeaway: Getting the trend back has been a reliable all-clear.

setups.title: Five straight up days
setups.takeaway: Short-term overbought — the market usually digests, rarely collapses.

setups.title: January finishes down (January barometer)
setups.takeaway: The old saying has failed lately: since 2010, down Januarys were bought more often than not.
